subsystems.name: Strange-matter bulk
subsystems.role: the hypothetical material itself: a self-bound droplet in which up, down and strange quarks are deconfined rather than locked inside protons and neutrons.
parts: up, down and strange quarks in roughly equal numbers

subsystems.name: Surface layer
subsystems.role: the boundary between the droplet and ordinary matter, which determines whether it is stable and whether it would convert surrounding nuclei.

subsystems.name: Production driver
subsystems.role: creates the extreme energy density in which deconfined quarks can form.

subsystems.name: Compression and containment
subsystems.role: would hold the material at the enormous pressure it may need to stay in this state.
parts: no demonstrated apparatus exists; a neutron star's gravity is the only known natural container

subsystems.name: Diagnostics
subsystems.role: detects and characterises any droplet that survives, to test whether the state exists at all.

buildSteps.title: Accelerate heavy ions
buildSteps.detail: Nuclei such as lead or gold are stripped of electrons and accelerated close to the speed of light in a ring collider.

buildSteps.title: Collide them
buildSteps.detail: Two beams are focused to collide head-on, concentrating energy into a volume a few femtometres across.

buildSteps.title: Form a quark-gluon plasma
buildSteps.detail: For about 10⁻²³ seconds the collision produces a hot, dense fireball in which quarks and gluons move freely — this has been done at RHIC and the LHC.

buildSteps.title: Let it cool and hadronise
buildSteps.detail: As the fireball expands it cools and quarks recombine into ordinary hadrons. Only if strange quark matter is the true ground state might some droplets survive instead.

buildSteps.title: Search for survivors
buildSteps.detail: Detectors and dedicated searches look for strangelets or other long-lived exotic fragments. None has been found in collider or cosmic-ray data so far.

buildSteps.title: Test stability at zero pressure
buildSteps.detail: The key open question is whether such a droplet would stay bound with no external pressure — only then could it exist as a bulk material.

buildSteps.title: Find a way to compress bulk matter
buildSteps.detail: To make it in quantity, ordinary matter would have to be squeezed to nuclear or higher densities. On Earth no known method reaches this; in nature only the interior of a neutron star might.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture a bulk form
buildSteps.detail: If stable material could be made at all, shaping it into sheets or shells would require handling a substance that may convert ordinary nuclei it touches — a step with no known engineering route.

prerequisites.why: the only machines that briefly create deconfined quark matter, at RHIC and the LHC.
the boundary between ordinary hadrons and quark matter is known only roughly, and the location of any strange-matter region is uncertain.

prerequisites.tech: Proof that strange quark matter is the ground state
prerequisites.why: this 1980s hypothesis is unconfirmed; without it, no droplet of this kind would be stable outside extreme pressure.

prerequisites.tech: Bulk compression or containment at nuclear density
prerequisites.why: nothing built can hold matter at the required pressure or density, which is why the material has never been made in bulk.

prerequisites.tech: Neutron-star observations to test the idea
prerequisites.why: measurements of neutron-star masses, radii and cooling can constrain whether strange matter exists inside them.

pathway.milestone: quark-gluon plasma routinely produced in heavy-ion collisions; strangelet searches return nothing
pathway.unlocks: experimental grounding for the theory, but no material.

pathway.milestone: tighter constraints from colliders and from neutron-star mass, radius and merger measurements
pathway.unlocks: a yes/no indication of whether strange matter is real and stable.

pathway.milestone: hypothetical detection of a stable strangelet, in cosmic rays or as a relic of a compact-object event
pathway.unlocks: a sample to study, and the first real test of the stability hypothesis.

pathway.milestone: a demonstrated route to bulk compression or self-sustaining conversion
pathway.unlocks: only then could any material use — including the hull-plating and vacuum-stability ideas sometimes attached to it — be assessed at all; today those are speculation, and vacuum stability is a separate question about the electroweak vacuum, not something a strange-matter shell would address.
